findings.title: Aliased count() columns silently bypass upsampling transform
findings.body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling matches column_lower == "count()" exactly. Any column with an explicit alias such as "count() as my_count" or even "count() as count" will not match and falls through to the else branch, which appends the original column unchanged. The endpoint code (organization_events_stats.py) now calls this transform on every y-axis column when upsampling is enabled, so a user who aliases their count column (e.g. for a chart with multiple y-axes) will silently get the raw count() while a user with no alias gets the upsampled value. The fix is to detect count() with optional "as <alias>" and replace the function name while preserving the alias, e.g. emit "upsampled_count() as my_count".

findings.title: topEvents error message changed, breaking API contract
findings.body: The 400 response for topEvents <= 0 was changed from {"detail": "If topEvents needs to be at least 1"} to {"detail": "topEvents needs to be at least 1"}. This is a user-visible API contract change. Any client or integration that matches the previous string (e.g. Sentry's own frontend, alert rules, or downstream tooling) will stop recognizing the error. Either keep the original wording or coordinate this with the frontend before merging.

findings.title: Tests mock options.get but do not clear the 60s upsampling cache
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects (error_upsampling.py) caches the boolean result of the allowlist check for 60 seconds using cache.get/set. The four new tests in test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects etc. patch sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options, but if any earlier test in the same run (or a prior test in this class) has populated the cache for the same organization+projects, the cached True/False is returned without re-running options.get and the mock has no effect. This can cause intermittent failures or false successes. The tests should reset the cache (e.g. via cache.clear() or invalidate_upsampling_cache) in setUp/tearDown before patching options.

findings.title: upsampled_count assumes sample_weight is non-NULL for every row
findings.body: The new upsampled_count SnQL aggregate is implemented as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). SQL/ClickHouse sum() ignores NULL values entirely, so any event in an allowlisted project that lacks sample_weight (e.g. older data, a partial backfill, or a schema mismatch) will be silently dropped from the count. The comment in error_upsampling.py asserts the column exists for all events, but nothing verifies it at query time, and the consequence is wrong downsampled charts that look valid. The aggregate should either coalesce NULLs (assume a weight of 1 for rows without sample_weight, or surface a null result) or the allowlist check should validate that backfill has actually completed.

findings.title: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling mutates all event types, not just errors
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling is invoked unconditionally inside store_event right after manager.get_data() for every event, and writes normalized_data["sample_rate"] whenever contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate is present. The function does not check the event type, so any transaction, attachment, or other non-error event that happens to carry an error_sampling context (whether by a SDK bug, a test fixture, or a future feature) will have sample_rate injected, potentially affecting other code paths that read sample_rate from those events. Guard the call on the event type being an error, or move the logic into the error-specific normalization path.

findings.title: Bare except Exception hides AttributeError/TypeError in sample rate extraction
findings.body: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling the first try/except wraps a chain of .get() calls on dicts, which never raise. The except Exception block is dead for the intended path but will silently swallow AttributeError or TypeError caused by a malformed normalized_data (e.g. contexts not being a dict). That makes a broken event manifest look like "no sample rate" instead of failing the test loudly. Catch only the specific exception you expect, or drop the try/except entirely around the .get() chain.

findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() of a tuple of ints
findings.body: The cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). While CPython's hash of a tuple of ints is deterministic within a given run, the contract relies on an internal implementation detail (the tuple hashing algorithm for nested ints) and produces a signed Python int that is concatenated into the key string. It would be safer and more portable to use an explicit deterministic digest (e.g. hashlib.md5 of the comma-joined sorted ids) so the cache key is stable across Python versions, implementations, and obvious to readers, and so cache busting via invalidate_upsampling_cache is reliable.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache has no test coverage
findings.body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is a public helper intended to be called when the allowlist changes, but no test in test_error_upsampling.py exercises it. Without a test, a future change to the cache key format (e.g. switching away from hash()) will silently break cache invalidation in production. Add a test that populates the cache, calls invalidate_upsampling_cache, and asserts cache.get returns None.

findings.title: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is not exercised
findings.body: The main public entry point is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects (which combines the allowlist check, the 60s cache, and the dataset/query filter) is never tested directly. The test file only covers the private helpers (_are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform, transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling). The caching behavior in particular is the riskiest new logic and should have a test that verifies a cache hit short-circuits the allowlist lookup.

findings.title: Redundant upsampling_enabled alias of should_upsample
findings.body: Inside _get_event_stats, should_upsample = is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...) is immediately followed by upsampling_enabled = should_upsample and the rest of the function only ever reads upsampling_enabled. The second variable adds no semantic value and makes the code look like the two could diverge. Drop one (preferably upsampling_enabled) and use should_upsample directly. (Noted as style rather than bug because there is no functional impact.)
